_note: iPhone companion rules. Same format, parser and scoring as the Android and desktop bundles; the 'ios' block is an iPhone extension that the Kotlin and Rust parsers ignore. Release values in ios.releases must be refreshed with every bundle release; the full indicator set is the separately signed ios-indicators.json.

rules.title: No passcode is set
rules.explain: Without a passcode, anyone who picks up this iPhone can read your messages, install a monitoring profile or change your Apple Account settings in a few minutes.

rules.title: An iOS update is waiting
rules.explain: Your iPhone is not on the newest release of its iOS version. Updates close the security holes that spyware uses to get in.

rules.title: This iPhone runs an older iOS version
rules.explain: Apple fixes most security problems first in the newest iOS version. If your iPhone can update to it, do.

rules.title: A profile or device management you don't recognise
rules.explain: A configuration profile can route your internet traffic through someone else's server, trust their certificates so they can read secure websites, and on a supervised iPhone, control the phone. Monitoring services use profiles because iPhone apps cannot spy on other apps.

rules.title: The profile is from your work or school
rules.explain: You said the profile was installed by your employer or school. They can see some activity on a managed iPhone, so ask them what it covers.

rules.title: Web traffic goes through a proxy
rules.explain: Your iPhone sends web traffic through a proxy server. Proxies are used by workplaces, but also to watch which websites someone visits.

rules.title: The proxy may come with your work or school profile
rules.explain: You said a profile on this iPhone is from your work or school, and such profiles often set a proxy. This explains the proxy only, nothing else the check finds. If you left that job or school, remove the profile.

rules.title: Signs this iPhone has been jailbroken
rules.explain: A jailbreak removes the iPhone's protections. Full-featured iPhone stalkerware needs one, so if you did not do this yourself, someone else may have had your phone.

rules.title: This iPhone is jailbroken
rules.explain: You said you jailbroke this iPhone yourself, so the traces are expected. A jailbroken iPhone has lost the protections that keep spyware out, and anything installed from jailbreak stores can read your messages, so this still counts against the phone.

rules.title: A debugger is attached to this app
rules.explain: Something is attached to Phone Spy Guard and could change what it shows you. Developers do this while testing; on a normal iPhone it should never happen.

rules.title: Apple sent you a threat notification
rules.explain: Apple only sends these when it believes mercenary spyware such as Pegasus was aimed at your account. Take it seriously even if nothing else looks wrong.

rules.title: Matches a published spyware indicator
rules.explain: A process in your iPhone's diagnostic records matches a name or path that researchers have published for mercenary spyware such as Pegasus.

rules.title: A program ran from a folder spyware uses
rules.explain: A program that delayed a restart was running from a hidden system folder where Apple's own software does not run, but where Pegasus, Reign and Predator infections have been found.

rules.title: A program ran from an unusual place
rules.explain: A program that delayed a restart was not part of iOS or an App Store app. This can have an innocent cause, so it is worth an expert's look rather than alarm.

rules.title: A program was running from a folder spyware uses
rules.explain: When the diagnostic archive was made, a program was running from a hidden system folder where Apple's own software does not run, but where Pegasus, Reign and Predator infections have been found.

rules.title: A program was running from an unusual place
rules.explain: When the diagnostic archive was made, a program was running that is not part of iOS or an App Store app. This can have an innocent cause, so it is worth an expert's look rather than alarm.

releases._note: Ordered oldest to newest; 'latest' is the newest iPhone build of each line, from https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100 on 2026-10-22. Refresh at every bundle release.

indicators.source: Core Pegasus names from Amnesty Tech (2021) and Kaspersky's shutdown.log research (2024); the full published set ships in the signed ios-indicators.json.
